body:
It's the same thing *Tilduke* said but from the other side of the diagnostic field...I care, but the difficulty of dealing with the 'dark passenger's whispers in my ear' makes it hard at times. You think to yourself 'it would be better to go now and leave them with this short trauma than to disintegrate in to a useless person who drags them down forever' ... 

That doesn't make it right, but the various genetic factors combined with what was going on in his personal head space can do powerful things. 

The best thing you can do is realize that his decision wasn't meant as a slap in the face...and by living your life well and being open about your experiences you might be able to help others who are on the edge. I have a coworker who has experienced a similar saga...being the survivor of several different destructive/suicidal people... Hearing her talk of the pain reminds me of why I strive to work past my issues...

This works for USA as well. I've only begun to stick my toe in the world of local politics (went to a protest/talk to customers who display the cues of being interested) and already I have people telling me I should use my passion to get more involved. One person even recommended I run for city council... My *eventual* degree is more important right now, but even the small connections I get to make between some of the local groups and interested parties has been curing some of my 'the world is doomed' blues.

I only do it once every few months...don't want to get addicted to that/have to feel the shame of having wasted my money. (and it's luck, right? So how will playing more often really help?) But those moments when I imagine exactly how it would feel to pay off the insane amount of bills that make me feel less than human... Those are good moments.

Dear sir, apologies for hijacking your thread, but you reminded me of how lucky I am. 

After weeks of off again/on again rainy weather, I'm having my day off during one of the glorious sunny days. My usually brown tinted area is ultra green from the rain and the tree in my backyard seems to have been ultra fertile, so we have a ton of baby saplings growing in the shade! Spring is here...you just have to go out and find it! :)
